non_blocking_findings: AC4 is only world-level determinism. A fresh capture-m4 here reproduced worlds.sha256 byte-for-byte against the public set (0 diff) but 12 of 15 PNG hashes differ from the public set and from the executor's (docked 01 frames and 07 match; 02-06 and 07 deck differ). Cause is visible: dust-flash ellipses and HUD card fade are not tick-deterministic (my 04_cruise_099_deck shows a full Archive card and no dust flashes; the report describes a half-faded card and several flashes). The report's 'public set byte-equal to local' is true only for the executor's own run. S1 sign-off should not assume pixel-reproducible frames; 'worlds' are the reproducible artefact.

AC8 deferral is honest and well evidenced: design spike p99 85 ms, executor 219 ms, my loaded run 498 ms, docked control p99 14-58 ms depending on load; bench fails loudly (MISS, rc 2) and nothing claims AC12 green. Caveat: under host load the same bench returns invalid (rc 1: 139 frames < 300) rather than MISS, and the Makefile collapses both to make rc 2 (message names the driver exit). A perf row must be run on a quiet rig; the bench's invalid-vs-MISS split is load dependent.

capture-m4-publish is not atomic: with worlds.sha256 missing it uploads 17 files before failing (P4); the pre-check validates PNGs and the png manifest only, not manifest.json/worlds.sha256 existence. Publishes to a public path.

Weak checks that survive mutation: contact-sheet layout is never verified (CB), cruise beta tolerance can be loosened 1e-12 -> 1.0 without failure (CC), removing dismiss_arrival changes nothing detectable (CA). The hand-edited tolerance has no tight negative test.

Renders show what the report lists as findings for S1 (not defects of this item): Earth/alpha Cen A discs clipped to flat white (01 forward, 06/07 forward), dust-impact ellipses at rest in 07 deck, ghosted Transit card under Arrived card, hull spire tip in every forward frame, cards cover ~30% of transit frames, cruise glow not a distinct feature (starbow core only).

Three executor hand edits to tools/ (beta tolerance, wall-time walk bounds, docked settle) are disclosed in commit and report; each is reasonable and the docked-settle one is what lets DC2 kill. Wall-time bounds slightly weaken determinism of walk timing but not of worlds.
